newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mostly higher, led by PGMs.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mostly higher, led by PGMs.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mostly higher Thursday, led by a jump in platinum group metals (PGMs) prices after news which suggested Russia may be changing its PGM marketing strategy, analysts said.
Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Chubais said Russia needed a new approach to raising revenue by sales of precious metals, equity issues, privatizations and alcohol taxes.
Chubais also said officials from Russia's central bank would resume PGM supply contract talks with Japan next week.
Russia is the world's largest supplier of palladium and supplies have been disrupted since December due to Russian fiscal and administrative problems.
But officials from the Russian central bank and finance ministry said they were unaware of Chubais's decision.
Meanwhile, reports suggested the Russian government was discussing with Swiss bank, UBS, a swap of stockpiled platinum and palladium for 30 tonnes of gold.
UBS is said to be holding 30 tonnes of Russian gold as collateral for a loan to the Russian government in 1995.
The deal may be worth more than $330 million and is seen possibly delaying further Russian PGM supply contracts with the Japanese.

"Russian stockpiles of platinum and palladium may be getting low, after a surge of exports last year, but the Russians still need to raise revenue, so maybe they figure it is better to conserve their PGM inventories and sell the gold instead," CPM Group New York analyst Ted Kempf said.
NYMEX July platinum ended up $6.60 at $378.40 an ounce after climbing a session peak of $384.50, the contract's highest level for a month.
Short-term platinum lease rates jumped to about six percent early Thursday, with Swiss houses seen big borrowers, refining sources said.
The October NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread soared to $31.00 an ounce, from $25.50 Wednesday, testing the highs seen in late February.
NYMEX June palladium ended up $2.50 at $153.50 after being limit up at $156.00 intraday.
Palladium lease rates remained firm around 8-10 percent for one month and 6-8 percent for three months.
Meanwhile, COMEX June gold ended up $1.00 at $344.30 after trading from $342.10 to $346.20. Estimated total volume for COMEX gold was a high 52,000 lots.

"This looks like it could be bullish scenario, with new fund shorts being forced to cover again, as lows for the year in gold may be in, but technically gold would need to climb back above $350 for the outlook to improve," said Scott Meyers, an analyst with Pioneer Futures, a New York COMEX clearing member.

Open interest in COMEX gold jumped a further 5,682 lots Wednesday to 165,092 contracts, after jumping 9,028 lots Tuesday, as funds began re-establishing short positions in the wake of Tuesday's lower-than-expected U.S. March CPI data.
But the four-year low in spot gold of $336.00 set in January have so far held during this week's slump, forcing some funds to buy back positions Thursday, analysts said.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted at $342.30/80 against the London afternoon fix of $340.40 and the New York close Wednesday around $341.00/50.
Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer on Thursday reiterated comments made Wednesday by German Finance Minister Waigel, saying Germany opposed central bank or IMF gold sales.
But Tietmeyer added it was not yet clear whether European central bank gold reserves would be transferred to the reserves of the planned European central bank under European Monetary Union.
European central banks hold about 14,300 tonnes of gold (460 million ounces), over 40 percent of all official world reserves.

COMEX Silver ended the session as the weakest performer today. May delivery lost 7.5 cents to settle at $4.695 after trading from $4.83 to $4.67. But so far, the low in spot silver of $4.70 posted earlier this month has held, traders noted.
